questions.stem: The polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 - x + 4\) has distinct integer roots. Which of the following is NOT a factor of the polynomial?
questions.hint: If \((x - a)\) is a factor then \(P(a) = 0\). The integer roots divide the constant term 4, so test \(\pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 4\). The factor whose root does NOT give 0 is the answer.

steps.explain: Write each factor as a root: \((x+1)\) → \(x = -1\);  \((x-1)\) → \(x = 1\);  \((x+4)\) → \(x = -4\);  \((x-4)\) → \(x = 4\). By the Factor Theorem, test \(P(\text{root}) = 0\).
So \((x + 4)\) is NOT a factor. (The three integer roots are \(-1,\ 1,\ 4\).)

keyPoints.note: Test integer divisors of the constant term.
Find the root that gives P ≠ 0.

y-coordinates from \(Q(x)\): \(Q(1)=2-7+3=-2\) and \(Q(3)=18-21+3=0\) (B on the x-axis ✓).

questions.stem: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2+mx+n=0\), find the roots of \(nx^2-mx+1=0\) in terms of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

questions.stem: One of the roots of the equation \(x^3+kx^2+1=0\) is the sum of the other two roots. Show that \(x=-\dfrac{k}{2}\) is a root of the equation.
questions.answer: Let the roots be α, β and α + β. The sum of the roots is α + β + (α + β) = 2(α + β) = −k, so α + β = −k/2. Since α + β is a root, x = −k/2 is a root.
questions.hint: Name the roots \(\alpha,\ \beta\) and \(\alpha+\beta\). Use the sum of the roots \(=-\dfrac{b}{a}\).

steps.explain: Let the roots be \(\alpha,\ \beta,\ \alpha+\beta\) (one root is the sum of the other two).
Sum of the roots of \(x^3+kx^2+0x+1=0\) is \(-k\).
But \(\alpha+\beta\) is itself a root, so \(x=-\dfrac{k}{2}\) is a root. ✓

keyPoints.note: Sum of the roots gives α + β directly.
